analysis.title: The great volatility disconnect
key_insights: Defensive sectors are showing bubble-like price action. BofA's Bubble Risk Indicator has healthcare and staples approaching extreme levels after the historic rotation into defensives, similar to dynamics seen in the dotcom bubble and post-Covid melt-up.
In the US, more than two-thirds of the S&P 500's top 50 stocks by market cap have recently delivered earnings moves larger than options implied, a 98th-percentile reading.

In Europe, only around one-third of stocks exceeded their implied earnings moves, despite an unusually elevated earnings premium. European investors have been paying up for moves that did not materialize.

Realized earnings moves have outpaced implied expectations, particularly among the largest index constituents, despite rising option premiums. Heading into megacap earnings, expensive-looking options have not been expensive enough.

BofA highlights SMH as offering one of the most attractive upside call-spread payouts among liquid ETFs that have sold off since the October 6 Nasdaq peak. December at-the-money call spreads targeting a one-standard-deviation rebound offered roughly 2.8x payout as of October 26.
With earnings, the Fed and midterms approaching, BofA sees the possibility of a post-catalyst risk-on reversal in semiconductors.
On the October 22 Nasdaq selloff of nearly 3%, US 10-year yields fell more than 16bps. AI weakness is increasingly trading like a growth shock rather than an inflation or rates shock.
The volatility gap between Nasdaq and the S&P 500 continues to widen. The next serious AI unwind could produce a different cross-asset response than the inflation-driven selloffs.
